summary: The system is managing unannounced meals using aggressive automation, but extremely high safety limits combined with delayed digestion from GLP-1 medications are leading to severe insulin stacking and dangerous late-phase and overnight hypoglycemia.
education: GLP-1 medications slow down gastric emptying, meaning carbohydrates take longer to raise blood glucose.
Max IOB and Max Basal limits act as the safety ceiling for your pump. If these are set too high, the system can deliver too much insulin during a spike before the delayed food has a chance to absorb.
A 3-minute SMB interval allows the algorithm to re-evaluate and deliver microboluses continuously, which can overwhelm the body's actual insulin need if meal absorption is slow.
strengths: Excellent CGM sensor adherence with 98.7% coverage over 14 days.
Strong Time in Range during morning and early daytime hours before evening meals occur.
Loop is actively tracking and attempting to correct glucose variations 24/7.
issues: Severe hypoglycemia risk overnight, reaching 18.5% Time Below Range during the 01:00 local hour.
Extreme automation limits (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) provide no effective safety ceiling.
The 3-minute SMB interval allows rapid insulin stacking before delayed meals can absorb.
Zero carbohydrate logging prevents the algorithm from matching insulin delivery to actual food size.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
Max IOB of 25 U is exceptionally high and dangerous for a total daily basal profile of ~15-20 U. Please consult your care team immediately about establishing safe Max IOB and Max Basal limits.
Extreme lows in the 40 mg/dL range were recorded on multiple days. Treat lows rapidly and consider temporarily reducing automation intensity while investigating.

analysis_steps.findings: Severe overnight and late-evening hypoglycemia is directly caused by a combination of unannounced meals, delayed GLP-1 digestion, and dangerously loose AAPS safety limits (Max IOB 25U, 3-min SMB interval). The system must be constrained before optimizing profile parameters.
analysis_steps.evidence: 18.5% TBR at 01:00. Max IOB 25 U. 3-minute SMB interval. GLP-1 notes.

recommendations.title: Tighten Max IOB and Max Basal Limits
recommendations.description: Current limits (Max IOB 25 U, Max Basal 12 U/h) are extremely dangerous and allow the system to stack massive amounts of insulin for unannounced meals, causing severe crashes. A safer Max IOB is generally 3x your largest typical meal bolus.

recommendations.title: Restore Safe SMB Interval
recommendations.description: An SMB interval of 3 minutes is too aggressive, especially with delayed digestion from GLP-1. Increasing it allows the system more time to evaluate whether previous insulin is working before delivering more.

recommendations.title: Raise Fasting/Overnight Target
recommendations.description: A target of 90 mg/dL provides almost zero safety buffer against the momentum of UAM insulin stacking. Raising the overnight target to 100 mg/dL (matching the daytime target) will reduce severe lows.

profile_recommendation.rationale: The 90 mg/dL target leaves insufficient buffer against momentum from UAM-driven SMBs, leading to frequent hypoglycemia in the 40s and 50s overnight. Aligning it to 100 mg/dL provides a safer cushion.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Monitor overnight Time Below Range for 3 days after tightening AAPS safety limits and raising the target.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Raise the 00:00 and 23:00 target segments from 90 mg/dL to 100 mg/dL.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS / max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: Current limits are exceptionally unsafe. 25 U IOB provides no safety ceiling for unannounced meals, causing extreme post-meal crashes.
Dynamic ISF is functioning as expected, but its aggressive nature requires the tighter Max IOB limits recommended above.
Standard absorption models are acceptable since no carbs are currently being logged.

meal_strategy_summary.rationale: The user relies on a 100% unannounced meal strategy, heavily dependent on UAM. Because GLP-1 delays digestion, the excessively loose safety limits (Max IOB 25 U) and 3-minute SMB interval dump insulin faster than food absorbs, causing late-phase severe lows.
meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Tighten AAPS safety limits immediately to prevent UAM from stacking dangerous amounts of insulin before delayed food absorbs.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Log the exact time and carbohydrate amount of one major daily meal for 3 days to determine true absorption delay without relying on UAM guessing.

implementation_steps: Consult your care team immediately to drastically reduce Max IOB and Max Basal limits to safe, physiological levels.
Increase the SMB interval from 3 minutes to at least 15 minutes to reduce rapid insulin stacking.
Raise the overnight (00:00 and 23:00) target to 100 mg/dL to add a safety buffer against lows.
Once safety limits are in place, begin logging the size and timing of meals in Nightscout so the algorithm can match delayed GLP-1 absorption more safely.
